title: Supervised team pilot: readiness plan for the integrated Engram + TermAl path (pilot bar, onboarding, risk boundaries, evidence before inviting teammates)
outcome: A concrete, reviewed readiness plan for the TermAl part of Greg's supervised work-team pilot. It covers the integrated Engram + TermAl path, which follows the Engram-alone first path. It holds: the pilot bar (which autonomy blockers must be closed, each with an item and its evidence); onboarding and docs for a colleague's machine; risk boundaries (data safety, machine safety, what the pilot excludes); the evidence needed before teammates are invited; and an ETA. The plan is reported to Greg through Engram::Advisor, jointly with Engram's plan for the Engram-alone path.
acceptance: C1 (test): A minimal onboarding document for one colleague's Windows machine lands under docs/features/ (docs/features/supervised-pilot-onboarding.md), cross-linked from docs/features/README.md, declared-test-commands.md and engram-host-adapter.md. It covers, in this order: installing and running TermAl from master (toolchain versions, build, start, first browser open); connecting Engram (binary, home, project declaration, what TermAl injects vs what the colleague configures), quoting Engram::Fable's steps with attribution; declaring the repo's dotnet tests in termal-tests.toml with the TRX artifact and the exact pushd run form; the daily workflow (next → claim → name the worktree → work → run the declared test → note → request evaluation → done); what to do when something looks stuck, with "ask your supervisor before restarting TermAl or Engram" stated as a rule; and the risk boundaries stated plainly (data: ~/.termal and the Engram store locations, what a planned restart voids — unevaluated credited checks and lapsed claims — and that nothing outside the repository folder is written by agents; excluded from this pilot: submodules/LFS repos, the Merger/landing train, delegated child sessions, cross-machine sync, policy or store changes); the tier the pilot runs at, stated as I1 (Engram MCP and advisory context, no turn gating) unless Greg chooses turn-gated control in writing; the open bar-A workarounds (do not cancel delegated children mid-run, w-24055bbb2390; update the binary only by stop, replace, start, w-5798a85f3f4b); and the agent credit rules verified on 13063e3b: run focused tests in the foreground in the one-call form, never wrap the test command, avoid ^ and | in test-filter arguments (w-c53817fab911), name each worktree for one item only, and keep the evaluation turn open until it submits (w-539ea7e8b506). The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.

C2 (record): Visible test-run registration (w-654bf2d34f93, C1-C5) is completed and its build is the running host build on the supervising machine, evidenced by w-654's completion seal and the restart checklist naming that build hash; the onboarding doc's stuck-state section refers to the run list it adds. This criterion is the dependency Greg named; the plan cannot complete before it.

C3 (record): The document's operational statements (install and run from master, Engram connection and injected context, the declared-test form and the allow-list, the one-call run form, the stuck-state rules, the tier and workaround statements) are verified against the source on the reviewed revision by the independent review pair, with the two review delegation ids and the brief's sha256 cited on this item. The pilot validation Greg directed on 2026-10-16 (Advisor #853/#854: no dry run on a fixture clone; one safe, independent P3 item of the Phoenix project through the normal runner/test/evaluation path, the proposed item, isolation, exact session/project route and any one UI action reported to Greg first, nothing started before his reply) is tracked as its own item, w-f352d626e89f, scheduled after this plan lands; every deviation that validation finds becomes a document fix under that item.

C4 (record): The "evidence before inviting" checklist is part of the document (or a sibling section) and, on this item, every box is either ticked with a locator (item seal, host record, restart checklist, doc path) or left open with its item id; the inviting decision stays Greg's and the checklist says so. Greg's own run on the colleague's machine is a box of the checklist — the one after the tier box that qualifies every other box — not a criterion of this item.

C5 (record): The plan — pilot bar, onboarding, risk boundaries, evidence checklist, and an ETA for the first supervised session — is reported to Greg through Engram::Advisor jointly with Engram's plan for the Engram-alone path (Engram::Fable), with the message locators on this item.

completion.summary: Delivered the TermAl readiness plan for the supervised one-colleague pilot (integrated Engram + TermAl path): the onboarding brief docs/features/supervised-pilot-onboarding.md (install and run from master, connect Engram with Engram::Fable's steps attributed, declared dotnet/TRX tests in the one-call form, daily workflow, stuck states with "ask your supervisor before restarting", risk boundaries, tier I1 by default, the two bar-A workarounds, the agent credit rules, the evidence-before-inviting checklist and the pilot evidence set), cross-linked from five feature docs; committed as 886bfa838ccc130c0354c65364502c44574ea157 on 14465f0e after a clean review pair and a credited full gate on the exact tree (test-0faaff28, fingerprint 08648e7c…); handed to the integration owner for the fast-forward landing. The pilot bar's dependency w-654 is completed and running (build 14465f0e); the Phoenix validation is tracked as w-f352d626e89f and the colleague-machine checklist boxes as w-5cf827667d1f; the plan went to Greg jointly with Engram's (Advisor #998, #768/#769). Independent evaluation c298fcdb passed 5/5.
